tamara_peopleops: pulling together the follow-ups from today's all-hands Q&A specifically about promotions, leveling, and comp. writing this as a short FAQ + manager scripts so teams can copy it into 1:1s and promo packets.

alexa_eng_mgr: ty! our managers want a clear rule on backdating promos (how far back can we set an effective date) and whether that affects RSU grants.

ben_total_rewards: short answers up front: backdating (retro) is allowed only up to the start of the current fiscal quarter and must be justified; retro pay follows payroll rules; existing RSU vest schedules are not rewritten by a promo. details below.

1) How far back can a promo be backdated?
- policy: effective dates can be backdated up to the first day of the current fiscal quarter (requires NOTE in packet with justification). Anything earlier needs executive approval.
- reason: limits accounting complexity and avoids grant/bonus recalculations across multiple quarters.

2) Retro pay mechanics (short)
- retro pay = pay back to the effective date. Payroll applies retro if approvals clear payroll cutoff. If cutoff missed, retro posts next pay period. Expect ~1 pay-period lag in most cases.

3) Does promotion change existing RSU schedules?
- no: current grants keep the original vesting schedule. If a new grant is part of the promotion, that grant is separate and will have its own schedule and approval memo.

4) Promo + Performance Improvement Plans (PIP) interactions
- if an employee is on a PIP, promotions are not automatic. Managers should attach a note explaining why promo is appropriate despite/alongside a PIP (evidence of sustained impact or corrected behavior). People Ops will route these for special review.

5) Off-cycle promotions vs standard review cycle
- we support off-cycle promos for clear business reasons. Managers should document timing rationale (retention, expanded scope, role change) in the packet. Total Rewards may request additional justification for comp adjustments outside normal cycles.

6) Who signs if manager is unavailable?
- first: skip-level manager. second: director. final: People Ops signs to avoid payroll blockage. Record who signed and why in the packet.

7) Announcement consent & timing
- default: internal announce is OK but ask the employee before making public posts. for sensitive moves (role changes that involve cross-org transitions), coordinate with People Ops for timing.

8) Manager script (short, neutral)
"Hi <name>, congrats 	6 we've approved a promotion to <new title> effective <date>. This reflects your work on <impact>. Payroll and People Ops will follow up with timing/details. I'm here for questions."

9) Manager script (on leave)
"Congrats <name>. We're promoting you to <new title> effective <date>. We'll complete paperwork while you are on leave and confirm compensation timing. We can discuss details when you're back if you'd prefer."

people-ops-bot: Promo packet template (compact) uploaded: https://drive.google.com/example-promo-compact (auto note)

tamara_peopleops: next steps: i'll draft a one-page "Promo Quick Guide" with the checklist + scripts + link to the template and post in #managers by EOD tomorrow. i'll also run a single 30-min office hour for packet QA next Wed. Reply here if you want a private slot.

ceo_sophie: thanks all 	6 appreciate the clarity and the PIP note.
drew_engineer: can we add an example packet (anonymized) to the one-pager? managers love examples.
tamara_peopleops: yes will include one anonymized example with redacted fields.
